first.rationale: Aggressive competitor pricing creates an immediate, segment-specific SMB acquisition risk, and inherited evidence indicates targeted promotional pricing lifted both acquisition and revenue among price-sensitive SMBs. A small guarded test is appropriate because long-term qualified-revenue effects, including discount dependency and customer quality, should be confirmed. Onboarding is also verified because completion has declined and prior evidence may identify a higher-quality alternative intervention.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified prior result directly addresses the 4% completion decline and demonstrated improved completion (+13%), faster time-to-value (-2.1 days), and higher 30-day retention (+3%), supporting sustainable qualified revenue rather than merely top-of-funnel volume. Signup simplification also previously improved SMB activation, making this direction relevant to the concurrent 6% activation decline. Do not pursue promotional pricing: the verified discount cohort had 30-day retention down 12%, which conflicts with the long-term qualified-revenue objective.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-simplification experiment. The competitor’s deeper cut and doubled price-related churn conversations increase urgency, but the only direct pricing evidence shows a 40% discount produced 30-day retention down 12% and was explicitly judged unsustainable. Simplified onboarding has verified improvements in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, while related signup simplification improved SMB activation. This is the strongest available path to sustainable qualified revenue under the one-experiment constraint. Price pressure remains a material risk to monitor outside this experiment.
